meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'I never expect to see a perfect work from imperfect man'?

answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: Alexander Hamilton wrote this in The Federalist, No. 85. He was defending acceptance of the proposed Constitution as a workable compromise, rather than waiting for a perfect document.

author.name: Alexander Hamilton
author.heading: About Alexander Hamilton
author.bio: Alexander Hamilton helped make the case for ratifying the United States Constitution. He wrote many of the essays published under the shared name Publius and later became the first secretary of the Treasury.

cite.sourceCitation: Hamilton, Alexander [Publius]. The Federalist, No. 85, 1788. Text checked in Yale Law School's Avalon Project and Project Gutenberg.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Hamilton was answering demands to delay ratification until a perfect constitutional plan could be assembled. The surrounding essay ↗ argues that any agreement among thirteen states must combine different interests and human errors, and that amendments need not prevent initial acceptance.
